1→# Design: CLI Config Editor & Daemon Mode
     2→
     3→## Overview
     4→
     5→Two features for OpenACP:
     6→1. **`openacp config`** — Menu-based interactive config editor
     7→2. **Daemon mode** — Background execution with auto-start on boot, chosen during onboarding
     8→
     9→## Config Schema Changes
    10→
    11→Add to `ConfigSchema`:
    12→
    13→```typescript
    14→runMode: z.enum(['foreground', 'daemon']).default('foreground')
    15→autoStart: z.boolean().default(false)
    16→```
    17→
    18→- `runMode: 'daemon'` — `openacp` spawns a background process and exits
    19→- `autoStart: true` — installs OS-level auto-start (LaunchAgent on macOS, systemd on Linux)
    20→- Env override: `OPENACP_RUN_MODE` (must be added to `applyEnvOverrides` in config.ts)
    21→
    22→## CLI Commands
    23→
    24→| Command | Description |
    25→|---|---|
    26→| `openacp` (no args) | Reads `runMode` from config. `foreground` → runs server directly. `daemon` → spawns detached child and exits. |
    27→| `openacp start` | Force daemon mode (regardless of config) |
    28→| `openacp stop` | Reads PID from `~/.openacp/openacp.pid`, sends SIGTERM |
    29→| `openacp status` | Checks PID file, reports running/stopped |
    30→| `openacp logs` | Reads `logDir` from config, tails `openacp.log` in that dir with `tail -f -n 50` |
    31→| `openacp config` | Menu-based config editor |
    32→| `openacp --foreground` | Force foreground (overrides `runMode: daemon`) |
    33→| `openacp --daemon-child` | Internal flag — actual server process spawned by daemon mode |
    34→
    35→### Daemon Spawn Logic
    36→
    37→1. Check `~/.openacp/openacp.pid` — if PID file exists but process is not alive, remove stale PID file. If process alive, print "Already running (PID xxx)" and exit
    38→2. Spawn `node <cli-path> --daemon-child` with `{ detached: true, stdio: 'ignore' }`
    39→3. **Parent** writes child PID to `~/.openacp/openacp.pid` (single writer — child does NOT write PID)
    40→4. Parent exits immediately
    41→
    42→### `--daemon-child` Behavior
    43→
    44→- Initializes pino logger before any output (structured JSON logs, consistent with existing format)
    45→- Redirects stdout/stderr to log file at configured `logDir` path
    46→- Runs `startServer()` as normal
    47→- On shutdown (SIGTERM): removes PID file
    48→
    49→### Foreground/Daemon Interaction
    50→
    51→- `openacp --foreground` does NOT write a PID file — it runs like the current behavior
    52→- `openacp start` and daemon-mode `openacp` always check/write PID file
    53→- `openacp stop` only affects daemon processes (PID file). Foreground processes are stopped with Ctrl+C as usual
    54→- If a foreground instance is running and user runs `openacp start`, the daemon starts independently (no conflict — they are separate processes)
    55→
    56→## Menu-based Config Editor
    57→
    58→### Flow
    59→
    60→```
    61→openacp config
    62→  → Main menu:
    63→    ❯ Telegram
    64→      Agent
    65→      Workspace
    66→      Security
    67→      Logging
    68→      Run Mode
    69→      ← Exit
    70→```
    71→
    72→Selecting a group shows current values and edit options:
    73→
    74→```
    75→[Telegram]
    76→  Bot Token: sk-xxx...xxx
    77→  Chat ID: -1001234567890
    78→
    79→  ❯ Change Bot Token
    80→    Change Chat ID
    81→    ← Back
    82→```
    83→
    84→### Edit Behavior
    85→
    86→- Shows current value as default
    87→- Enter to keep current, or type new value
    88→- Validates same as setup (bot token → API check, chat ID → supergroup check)
    89→- After editing a field → returns to group menu
    90→- Back → returns to main menu
    91→- Exit → saves config to disk
    92→- Ctrl+C at any point → discards unsaved changes (same as existing setup wizard's `ExitPromptError` handling)
    93→
    94→### Run Mode Submenu
    95→
    96→```
    97→[Run Mode]
    98→  Current: foreground
    99→  Auto-start: off
   100→
   101→  ❯ Switch to daemon
   102→    ← Back
   103→```
   104→
   105→- "Switch to daemon" → sets `runMode: 'daemon'`, installs OS service, sets `autoStart: true`
   106→- "Switch to foreground" → sets `runMode: 'foreground'`, removes OS service, sets `autoStart: false`
   107→- "Toggle auto-start" → independently toggle `autoStart` (install/remove OS service without changing `runMode`)
   108→
   109→Users can run daemon mode without auto-start, or enable auto-start independently.
   110→
   111→## Auto-start on Boot
   112→
   113→### macOS (LaunchAgent)
   114→
   115→File: `~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.openacp.daemon.plist`
   116→
   117→```xml
   118→<plist version="1.0">
   119→<dict>
   120→  <key>Label</key>
   121→  <string>com.openacp.daemon</string>
   122→  <key>ProgramArguments</key>
   123→  <array>
   124→    <string>/path/to/node</string>
   125→    <string>/path/to/openacp/cli.js</string>
   126→    <string>--daemon-child</string>
   127→  </array>
   128→  <key>RunAtLoad</key>
   129→  <true/>
   130→  <key>KeepAlive</key>
   131→  <true/>
   132→  <key>StandardOutPath</key>
   133→  <string>/Users/username/.openacp/logs/openacp.log</string>
   134→  <key>StandardErrorPath</key>
   135→  <string>/Users/username/.openacp/logs/openacp.log</string>
   136→</dict>
   137→</plist>
   138→```
   139→
   140→- Install: `launchctl load <plist>`
   141→- Uninstall: `launchctl unload <plist>` + delete file
   142→
   143→### Linux (systemd user service)
   144→
   145→File: `~/.config/systemd/user/openacp.service`
   146→
   147→```ini
   148→[Unit]
   149→Description=OpenACP Daemon
   150→
   151→[Service]
   152→ExecStart=/path/to/node /path/to/openacp/cli.js --daemon-child
   153→Restart=on-failure
   154→
   155→[Install]
   156→WantedBy=default.target
   157→```
   158→
   159→- Install: `systemctl --user daemon-reload && systemctl --user enable openacp`
   160→- Uninstall: `systemctl --user disable openacp` + delete file
   161→
   162→### Platform Detection
   163→
   164→`process.platform === 'darwin'` → launchd, `'linux'` → systemd.
   165→
   166→### Windows
   167→
   168→Daemon mode and auto-start are not supported on Windows. If `runMode: 'daemon'` is set on Windows, fall back to foreground with a warning. The onboarding step will not show the daemon option on Windows.
   169→
   170→### Path Expansion
   171→
   172→All paths in generated service files (plist, systemd) must use absolute paths via `os.homedir()`. Tilde (`~`) is NOT expanded by launchd or systemd.
   173→
   174→## Onboarding Changes
   175→
   176→Add Run Mode as step 3 (Workspace becomes step 2):
   177→
   178→```
   179→[3/3] Run Mode
   180→
   181→  How would you like to run OpenACP?
   182→
   183→  ❯ Background (daemon)
   184→    Runs silently, auto-starts on boot.
   185→    Manage with: openacp status | stop | logs
   186→
   187→    Foreground (terminal)
   188→    Runs in current terminal session.
   189→    Start with: openacp
   190→```
   191→
   192→- **Background** → `runMode: 'daemon'`, `autoStart: true` → install OS service → spawn daemon → print "OpenACP is running in background (PID xxx)"
   193→- **Foreground** → `runMode: 'foreground'`, `autoStart: false` → start server directly (current behavior)
   194→
   195→Step numbering updates: `[1/3] Telegram` (includes bot token + group chat as before), `[2/3] Workspace`, `[3/3] Run Mode`. Agent detection remains non-interactive (auto-detect, print result) — no step header needed.
   196→
   197→## New Files
   198→
   199→| File | Purpose |
   200→|---|---|
   201→| `src/core/daemon.ts` | Spawn logic, PID management, start/stop/status |
   202→| `src/core/autostart.ts` | LaunchAgent/systemd install/uninstall |
   203→| `src/core/config-editor.ts` | Menu-based config editor |
   204→
   205→## Dependencies
   206→
   207→No new dependencies. Uses existing `@inquirer/prompts` and Node.js built-ins (`child_process`, `fs`).
   208→

    23→  openacp --version                    Show version

    48→        core.registerAdapter(channelName, adapter)

    50→      } else {
    51→        const name = channelName
    52→        const err = channelConfig.adapter

But wait—on macOS, all plists in `~/Library/LaunchAgents/` are automatically loaded at login regardless of prior unload state, so I need a different approach. I could use a "desired state" file that the daemon checks on startup, or I could leverage launchd's native `PathState` functionality to only keep the process alive when a file exists. The second option is cleaner since it uses launchd's built-in features rather than custom logic. So I'll skip `RunAtLoad` and instead use `KeepAlive.PathState` — when `openacp start` creates the run file, launchd will automatically start the process, and when `openacp stop` removes it, launchd will stop the process.
